title: scan() silently drops all blocks after first decode error in a block
description: Trigger: a multi-block input where one block has a corrupt data line, followed by a valid block. In handle_block, the Err(_) arm breaks out of the data-line loop without updating scan_pos. end_offset is initialized to input.len() and is never updated (found_end stays false). After the break, *pos = end_offset = input.len(), which causes the outer scan_impl loop to exit immediately. All blocks after the corrupt block are silently dropped. The doc promises 'scanner continues past the offending construct' but this only applies to begin-base64 and malformed begin lines, not decode errors. Callers scanning a Usenet archive body expecting all blocks will get only the blocks up to and including the first bad one. Fix: when breaking on Err(_), advance scan_pos = le (past the bad line), then set *pos = scan_pos rather than *pos = end_offset.
close_reason: Fixed: in handle_block Err(_) arm, now sets end_offset=le before break so *pos advances past the bad line, allowing subsequent blocks to be scanned.
